### Scores
- Correctness & Rigor: 4 — Consensus algorithm is proven, but the leader-election timeout is unvalidated
- Performance & Efficiency: 3 — Write amplification triples under the proposed replication factor
- Security: 4 — mTLS between nodes, though certificate rotation is manual
- Technical Consistency: 4 — Matches the existing service mesh topology

### Overall Analysis
The replication design rests on Raft, whose safety properties are formally proven — that part of the claim holds. The unverified assertion is the 150ms leader-election timeout, which the proposal carries over from a single-region benchmark and applies to a three-region deployment where p99 inter-region latency alone reaches 90ms. Write amplification at replication factor 3 was measured on the vendor's published benchmark, not on this workload. Manual certificate rotation is the operational weak point. A measured election timeout under real cross-region latency would change my verdict.

### Verdict
Conditional Approval (measure leader-election timeout under production cross-region latency before rollout)

### Risks and Concerns
- Leader-election timeout inherited from a single-region benchmark; cross-region p99 latency alone consumes 60% of the budget
- Write amplification at RF=3 measured on vendor benchmark, not on this write pattern
- Certificate rotation is manual — expiry becomes a cluster-wide outage
- No documented procedure for recovering from a partitioned quorum

### References
- Raft consensus paper (Ongaro & Ousterhout, 2014)
- Vendor replication benchmark, 2026-05 release notes
